papers.title: CAMINOS reference model, Fig. 1
papers.citation: Tahvili, Vinck and di Volo, PLoS Comput Biol 2026
papers.question: Does the E–PV–SOM AdEx network give about 35 Hz gamma, SOM after PV, PV > SOM > E and an onset above a critical p?
papers.verdict_note: under v7 (amended after v6 R4 failed)
papers.summary: Gamma, the PV→SOM lag and the rate order reproduce at p = 0.07. The critical-p onset (Fig. 1E) runs in reverse with the external drive fixed at 560 sources (v6) and appears at p = 0.04 with the drive at p·NE sources (v7), an assumption the paper does not state for the sweep. At p = 0.07 the v6 and v7 runs are identical for all five seeds, so R1–R3 and R4v7 score one realization there.

criteria.claim: the network oscillates at about 35 Hz
criteria.estimand: peak frequency f_pk of the E rate spectrum, seeds 1–5 at p = 0.07

criteria.claim: SOM fires after PV within each cycle, about 8.5 ms
criteria.estimand: lag of the PV→SOM rate cross-correlation peak, mean over seeds
criteria.criterion: lag positive in every seed, mean 6–11 ms

criteria.claim: rates order PV > SOM > E, E at 1–3 Hz
criteria.estimand: mean rate per population over the kept 10 s
criteria.criterion: PV > SOM > E in every seed, mean E 1–3 Hz

criteria.claim: oscillations appear above a critical p (Fig. 1E)
criteria.estimand: oscillation at p = 0.02–0.10, seeds 1–3, drive 560 sources
criteria.criterion: no seed oscillates at p = 0.02; all seeds oscillate at p = 0.07
criteria.value_label: smallest p where all seeds oscillate
criteria.reason: every run oscillates, p = 0.02 included; peak excess is largest at low p

criteria.claim: oscillations appear above a critical p (Fig. 1E)
criteria.estimand: as R4, with drive round(p·NE) sources
criteria.criterion: no seed oscillates at p = 0.02 while E fires (≥ 0.1 Hz); all seeds oscillate at p = 0.07
criteria.value_label: smallest p where all seeds oscillate
criteria.reason: at p = 0.03, 2 of 3 seeds fail only the 20 Hz band-edge rule (f_pk 22 Hz, peak excess 22–26)

sensitivity.label: float64
sensitivity.note: every value inside the seed range; f_pk moves 1 Hz from seed 1, equal to the seed range and the 1 Hz grid step

sensitivity.label: dt 0.05 ms
sensitivity.note: every shift inside the seed range

sensitivity.label: fixed in-degree
sensitivity.note: small shifts past the seed range (f_pk +1 Hz; E, PV and lag slightly low); R1–R3 bands still met

sensitivity.label: shared drive (560 trains at p)
sensitivity.note: a cell sees about 39 sources instead of 560, so the drive falls 14-fold and E is silent; shared input remains untested

sensitivity.label: Brian2 step order
sensitivity.note: small shifts past the seed range (E, PV and SOM slightly high); R1–R3 bands still met

charts.title: Oscillation strength against p
charts.caption: Peak excess of the E rate spectrum per run; a run oscillates above 4. Lines join one seed across p.

charts.title: Population rates against p
charts.caption: Mean rates over the kept 10 s, seeds 1–3.

charts.title: Reference point p = 0.07, seeds 1–5
charts.caption: Peak frequency per seed at the reference point.

open: R4v7 rests on the drive scaling as p·NE across the sweep; the paper does not state it.
With the drive fixed at 560 sources (v6), every p oscillates; the onset needs the drive to scale with p. Shared-drive variant dropped (Hamm 2026-10-12).

papers.title: Predictive coding light, Fig. 3 (simple and complex cell tuning)
papers.citation: N'dri, Barbier, Teulière and Triesch, Nat Commun 2025
papers.question: Do the trained network's simple and complex cells show the paper's orientation, spatial-frequency and phase tuning?
papers.summary: Orientation tuning and the simple/complex phase split reproduce; sf tuning is broad (R_sf about 1.5 against 2) and complex cells show no frequency doubling.

R_ori ≥ 2 and above both null 99th percentiles
R_sf ≥ 2 and above both null 99th percentiles
criteria.reason: above both nulls, under the ratio of 2

criteria.criterion: R_sf ≥ 2 and above both null 99th percentiles
criteria.reason: above both nulls, under the ratio of 2

criteria.estimand: median excess modulation X (per trial, Poisson null)

criteria.claim: complex cells frequency-double, simple cells do not
criteria.criterion: median L simple < 0 < median L complex, difference above its null 99th
criteria.reason: complex median below 0; the set difference beats its null

sensitivity.label: lateral and top-down maps zeroed
sensitivity.note: T1 and simple T3 fail: the maps matter, so map order is not excluded

sensitivity.label: preferences on all phases
sensitivity.note: the fold does not explain T2

charts.title: T1 and T2 ratios against nulls and criterion
charts.caption: Held-out ratios with the 99th percentiles of both nulls (1000 draws).

charts.title: T3 phase modulation and T4 frequency doubling
charts.caption: T4 needs median L complex above 0.

charts.title: R_sf across sensitivity runs
charts.caption: R_sf stays under 2 in every variant.

open: The authors compute neither an sf selectivity index nor F1/F0; T2's ratio and T4's log ratio are the prereg's (diagnostic, unscored).
21 % of complex cells prefer the lowest tested sf.
The authors' tuning-curve data archive is not opened (Hamm's call).

papers.title: Predictive coding light, Fig. 2 (inhibitory STDP removes predictable spikes)
papers.citation: N'dri, Barbier, Teulière and Triesch, Nat Commun 2025
papers.question: Are learned inhibitory weights and spike suppression ordered by predictability?
papers.summary: Weights and suppression are ordered 1 > 2 > 3 in every network on the standalone model (P0) and on the jaxfne HDP kernel with the time-averaged weight (K0b); the end-of-epoch weight fails in 1 of 3 networks (K0). The paper's Fig. 2d values were not available, so there is no numerical comparison.
open: A scored comparison needs the paper's Fig. 2d values.

papers.title: Hodgkin–Huxley reference against a reduced jaxfne neuron (AT-01)
papers.question: How closely does a reduced jaxfne neuron follow a Hodgkin–Huxley cell under the same current step?
papers.summary: Rate agrees; peak voltage, resting voltage and first-spike time are outside the tolerances declared before the run.
open: One run; each arm fires one spike in 50 ms.

papers.title: Q-learning on jaxfne network features
papers.question: Can a linear Q-learner on network spike counts learn the optimal policy of chain5 and corridor7?
papers.summary: Network features reach and hold the corridor7 policy in 5 of 5 seeds, later than tabular (222–486 episodes against 2–23) with about a third of its Q error; the flat control never learns it.
open: Why the network code has lower Q error is untested (no ablation).

papers.title: Izhikevich 2003, Figs. 2 and 3 (single-cell patterns and the 1000-cell network)
papers.question: Does jaxfne's existing Izhikevich kernel reproduce the paper's single-cell firing patterns (Fig. 2) and the 1000-cell network rhythm (Fig. 3)?
papers.summary: P1 source and P2 port spec done (second review PASS 2026-10-12). The P3 preregistration is drafted and waits for its calibration gate and Hamm's signature; nothing is scored yet.
open: P3: calibration gate on synthetic signals, then the batch signature.
P4: build the scored arm and the NumPy reference arm (S1).
